rows.notes: The study is a narrative review of UAS applications in wildlife science combined with a systematic bibliometric review of wildlife journal records (counts of articles mentioning aircraft, satellites, tracking devices). It reports no original observations on wildlife disturbance from UAV flights; the disturbance statements (Section 2.4) are a synthesis of other studies (Sarda-Palomera 2012, Chabot 2015, Ditmer 2015, Vas 2015, etc.) concluding low to no disturbance from overflights but stronger reactions to close-up flights. Nothing in the study concerns lithium-ion battery disposal. Because it is a review, Q1 is no and all subsequent questions are no.
